topic: Dynamic stability: longitudinal and lateral, Phugoid, Dutch roll, Fixed wing autorotation
syllabus_extract: Dynamic stability: longitudinal and lateral, Phugoid, Dutch roll, Fixed wing autorotation. Short period oscillation, spiral divergence and Directional divergence.
specific_objectives: 11.1.4.1 Trainee will be able to describe aircraft stability in all the three axis

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of stability axes diagrams; Instructor supervision required for diagram interpretation
intro_questions: Define static stability in longitudinal axis.
List the three axes of aircraft motion.
Explain the difference between static and dynamic stability.

development.content:
Longitudinal dynamic stability definition
Short period oscillation characteristics
Phugoid oscillation characteristics
Lateral dynamic stability definition
Dutch roll oscillation characteristics

Spiral divergence characteristics
Directional divergence characteristics
Fixed wing autorotation principles
Comparison of oscillatory modes
Stability criteria summary

Application of stability concepts
Analysis of flight envelope limits
Review of dynamic modes
Instructor clarification of doubts
Preparation for next lesson

summary_questions: Describe the nature of the Phugoid oscillation.
Differentiate between Dutch roll and Spiral divergence.
Explain the role of fixed wing autorotation in stability.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on the relationship between longitudinal stability and the Short Period oscillation for the next lesson on Low speed wind tunnel testing.

pft_rows.syllabus: Low speed wind tunnel and wind tunnel balances. Demonstration on pressure plotting experiments. Measurements of lift and drag in wind tunnel.
